requirement:
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.

A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
rationale:
Judged against the text of `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The four marked tests in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs` cover each obligation.

I read `fn[exceptions]` only to see how exception identity is keyed. It keys exceptions by project-relative (file, item) and validates each through the shared citation-review path. It has no separate branch for file-level versus function-level exceptions.

- **Exceptions only through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence.**
  - `missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report` checks that a missing review fails the report with "missing citation review; run `habeas author`".
  - The same test checks that adding a review with a true determination makes the report pass.
  - `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution` checks that a review with determination `false` fails ("determination is false").
  - That test also checks that a `{fixme}` determination is rejected ("cannot accept a {fixme}").
  - These cases also cover "a source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count": a cite comment with no accepted review leaves `#fn[a]: zero execution` unexcused.
- **An exception may satisfy an unmet file threshold, an unexecuted function or a not-measured function.** `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution` checks all three:
  - "file threshold (0/1 (0.0%))" is listed under accepted exceptions;
  - "#fn[a]: zero execution" is accepted;
  - "#fn[a]: not measured" is accepted;
  - "code.rs: not measured — accepted exception" is accepted for a file that was not measured at all.
  - The same test checks that the exception does not raise execution coverage (still "0/1 (0.0%)").
  - It also checks that an unneeded citation does not break a passing report.
- **A file-threshold exception does not automatically excuse untested functions.** In the first part of `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution`, the file-level exception is accepted but `result.passed` is false and "#fn[a]: zero execution" is still reported.
- **An exception does not excuse another item.** `function_explanations_never_transfer_to_other_functions_or_the_file` checks:
  - An outer-function exception does not waive the nested inner function or a sibling function.
  - An inner-function exception does not waive the outer function or a sibling.
  - A function exception does not waive the file threshold ("code.rs: 0/1 (0.0%) — FAIL").
  - A function exception does not waive another file ("driver.rs: not measured — FAIL").
- **Invalidation on changes to the source item or justification.** `missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report` checks that changing the rationale text yields "citations changed" and the function is no longer excused. It also checks that changing the function body yields "outline input changed" and the gap is reported again. `standard_inline_doc_and_fenced_commentary_reviews_track_their_explanations` checks the same for an inline doc comment (reachable/inaccessible edit) and for a fenced commentary edit.
- **Portable identities.**
  - In `standard_inline_doc_and_fenced_commentary_reviews_track_their_explanations`, the review file is copied into a different temp-dir checkout and still validates as accepted with no errors.
  - Across reports in `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution` and `missing_and_stale_explanations_fail_the_report`, run labels and timestamps change (`record(..., 1/2/3 ...)`) while exception identity (`code.rs#fn[a]`) stays matched.

Staleness of a cited declaration is not tested with the exceptions subject. It comes from the shared citation-review validation, which `requirements.references.citation_review` and its own tests cover. A file-level exception going stale was not tested separately. Both go through the same validation path with no file/function branch, so I did not treat this as a gap. I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: :::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
:::{req} citation_review
Every source item outside the book that carries at least one `{cite}` reference
other than a citation of `habeas:util` under {cite}`requirements.references.util`
MUST have a citation review: an assessment of that item's citations, recorded at
`evidence/citations/<file>/<selector>.json`, where `<file>` is the item's
project-relative path, `<selector>` is its outline selector with every `/` and
`%` percent-encoded, and the root node uses `_root`. The review MUST use the
prompt defined by {cite}`requirements.authoring.citation_prompt`. For citations
of project requirements and examples, the reviewer MUST assess whether the item
should be re-checked or kept in sync when the cited definition changes, and
whether the reference procedure of
{cite}`requirements.references.procedure` calls for `{impl}` or `{test}` instead.
For citations of built-ins, the reviewer MUST check the permitted reference
roles and forms and any citation-review criteria stated in the built-in's fixed
text, using the item's source and commentary. A permitted citation role alone
MUST NOT suffice when the fixed text states additional criteria. Mandatory inputs,
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, MUST be the item's outline
node, each cited declaration or built-in text, and the citations' commentary. The record MUST contain the item's file and selector,
its citations by role, name, and commentary, `determination`, `rationale`, and
`inputs`, with determinations under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`. Validation
MUST require a current, accepted review for every such item and report stale,
missing, or orphaned reviews; a review MUST become stale when the item's hash,
a cited declaration, or its citations or their commentary change. Authoring with
`--all` MUST include citation reviews, and `habeas author citations:<file>#<selector>`
MUST author the review of the one item it names, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`, where omitting `#<selector>`
names the file's root node. A citation in a requirement or example
declaration is reviewed as part of that definition's own assessment instead.
Fenced commentary elsewhere in the book is reviewed under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review.book_commentary`.
Storage MAY use the versioned representation under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.habeas.evidence_format`, retaining the same review
information and validation rules.
